question: What percentage of an adult's total body weight does blood typically represent?
explanation: Blood accounts for approximately eight percent of total body weight in a healthy adult human. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T1#GNS111_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why do nurses check lab blood tests for patients?

options.A: To check if heart valves are working
options.B: To figure out exact daily fluid needs
options.C: To spot hidden problems and check if treatments are working

explanation: You'll see this every day in the ward! Blood tests help us catch underlying health issues and see how well our nursing and medical care is working. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T1#GNS111_U2_T1_h1)

question: What percentage of total blood volume does plasma normally constitute?
explanation: Plasma is the liquid extracellular matrix of blood and makes up about 55 percent of total volume. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T1#GNS111_U2_T1_h2)

question: What makes up the thin 'buffy coat' layer when blood spins in a centrifuge?
explanation: When blood spins down, the tiny buffy coat sits right in the middle, packed with our infection fighters (white cells) and clotting helpers (platelets)! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T1#GNS111_U2_T1_h2)

question: Which plasma protein keeps fluid inside our blood vessels through osmotic pressure?
explanation: Think of albumin as a sponge in the blood! It's the most abundant protein and holds onto water to keep blood pressure stable. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T1#GNS111_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is the main job of electrolytes like sodium and potassium in our blood plasma?

options.B: Carrying oxygen straight to body tissues
options.D: Keeping body pH balanced and helping cells send electrical signals

explanation: Electrolytes do much more than keep us hydrated—they keep our body fluids balanced and our nerves and muscles firing properly! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T1#GNS111_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary physiological function of mature erythrocytes in circulation?
explanation: Erythrocytes contain hemoglobin, which binds oxygen in the lungs and releases it in peripheral capillary beds. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T1#GNS111_U2_T1_h4)

question: Which part of our blood is actually just tiny cell pieces rather than whole cells?
explanation: Fun fact: platelets aren't whole cells at all! They are little fragments broken off from giant bone marrow cells to help us stop bleeding. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T1#GNS111_U2_T1_h4)

question: In an adult, where are most new blood cells made?
explanation: Red bone marrow acts as the ultimate factory inside our bones, churning out fresh blood cells every single day. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T1#GNS111_U2_T1_h5)

question: What hormone tells the body to make more red blood cells when oxygen levels drop?
explanation: When your kidneys sense low oxygen (hypoxia), they release erythropoietin (EPO) to speed up red blood cell production in the bone marrow. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T1#GNS111_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is the very first thing a blood vessel does when it gets cut or damaged?

options.D: The blood vessel spasms and squeezes shut

explanation: Right away, the smooth muscle in the damaged vessel wall clamps down (vascular spasm) to quickly slow down bleeding before a clot even forms. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T1#GNS111_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is the final result of the blood clotting cascade?

options.D: Turning fibrinogen into tough, tangled threads of fibrin

explanation: The clotting cascade finishes by weaving a strong net of fibrin fibers that locks the platelet plug firmly in place. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T1#GNS111_U2_T1_h6)

question: What condition happens when the blood cannot carry enough oxygen to the body's tissues?
explanation: Anemia means a lack of healthy red blood cells or hemoglobin, which is why patients often feel very tired and short of breath. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T1#GNS111_U2_T1_h7)

question: What signs would you expect to see in a patient with a very low platelet count (thrombocytopenia)?

options.B: Swollen legs and sudden weight gain
options.C: Tiny red spots, easy bruising, and bleeding that won't stop easily

explanation: Without enough platelets, the body can't form normal clots, leading to little spots called petechiae, easy bruising, and prolonged bleeding. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T1#GNS111_U2_T1_h7)
